hook: SCP-437 is short, and nearly all of its weight sits in two documents near the end: a friendly interview with a woman who once went to summer camp, and an email that follows it. Read the interview slowly, because the subject's cheerful nostalgia is doing more work than it seems. The article involves the bodies of teenagers and is quietly grim rather than graphic.
whyItMatters: It is a compact example of a file that hides its horror in the gap between two records. The containment section already hints that something is off, ordering a task force to detain persons of interest together with their children, and the article never fully explains why. Closing on a researcher's personal email instead of a formal conclusion gives the last word a human, uneasy tone.
thingsToNotice: The twist is that the adults who attended Camp Lakewood in 1991 are not the campers at all. Imaging finds deformed skeletons of 13-to-16-year-olds woven into every one of the 64 trees, organs still half working, and dental records match some of them to the original children, while a bur oak in the grove is identified as the real Samantha Blanchette. That recasts her interview: the 'best summer ever', the first kiss and the insistence that she never visited the grove read as a borrowed life, and her silence before that answer is the only crack in the act. Soon after, she slips out of custody and every other person of interest goes missing. The campfire legend she laughs off turns out to be literal, since Dr. Weiss confirms the children can still be heard through the bark after twenty years, which is why he raises euthanizing them.
